body_markdown:
Retro styling is the unofficial theme of this year’s Paris auto show (held October 12–18). Citroën unveiled a 2CV-inspired concept, Peugeot presented a concept that echoes the rally-winning 205 T16, and Renault-owned Alpine brought the little-known A310 into the 21st century. Debuting 55 years after the original A310, the new Alpine A310 Vision Concept could preview a new sports car.


Measuring about 179 inches long, 80 inches wide, and merely 46 inches tall, the A310 Vision is bigger than the original in every direction, yet its wedge-shaped silhouette looks like it was beamed directly from the 1970s. Alpine explains that its design team started the project by parking an example of the original A310 in the middle of its studio and using the coupe as a source of inspiration.


The idea wasn’t to copy and paste the past, so the A310 Vision isn’t entirely old-school. It gets so-called “pop-down” headlights, a semi-transparent roof panel, and blade-shaped rear lights positioned above a massive diffuser. The punched-out wheel arches remind us of the ones fitted to the V-6-powered A310, while the wheels, with their unusual “cut-out” look, recall the rims fitted to its 1970s predecessor.

Interior photos aren’t available yet, but Alpine notes that the cabin is decked out with physical buttons “inspired by the world of Hi-Fi.” Put another way, it sounds like the oh-so-1970s style that characterizes the exterior design permeated the interior as well.


The original A310 went on sale in 1971 with a rear-mounted four-cylinder engine, and a V-6-powered model joined the range for 1976. Fast-forward to 2026, and the A310 Vision is powered by an electric drivetrain. Alpine hasn’t released technical details, but it says that the concept is built on the new Alpine Performance Platform (APP) architecture designed to underpin a production-bound EV. The platform is rear-wheel-drive in its standard configuration, and it makes extensive use of aluminum to keep weight in check.


What’s next for the Alpine A310 Vision? Good question. Officially, the concept was built as “a creative exploration of Alpine’s heritage rather than the announcement of a future production model.” Don’t cue the sad trombone just yet. We know that a replacement for the A110 is in the pipeline, and the A310 Vision could hint at the styling direction it will take.


It’s a strategy that would make sense.[The modern A110](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/alpines-new-a110-again-taunts-us-from-afar/) released in 2017 was inspired by[the original A110](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/valuation/1961-77-alpine-a110-packs-a-rally-pedigree-and-french-charisma/) launched in 1962. If we assume that its replacement will land in 2027 or 2028, so a decade later, and that Alpine wants to keep offering a coupe with retro flair, it stands to reason that the new model’s styling will leap forward by a decade as well to appeal to younger enthusiasts.


Regardless of what it looks like, the A110’s successor could be sold in the United States. Alpine’s debut on the American market has been delayed, but the brand[still wants to sell cars here](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/alpine-still-wants-to-bring-the-a110-to-the-united-states/) . Its range will include SUVs, inevitably, and at least one sports car.
